title: ZeroDivisionError in divide()
author: Aman Samriya
symptom: The function divide(a, b) crashes when b = 0.
root_cause: No validation before dividing; Python raises ZeroDivisionError.
reasoning: Python evaluates a / b -> raises exception
tests:
def test_divide():
    assert divide(10, 2) == 5
    assert divide(10, 0) is None
    assert divide(0, 5) == 0
prevention: Add unit tests for edge cases
Return safe defaults or raise custom exceptions
impact: Program crash when invalid input is provided
summary: Adding input validation and graceful fallback prevents crashes and improves reliability.
